title: Follow-it button closes the table sheet even when main_open fails
body:
## Summary
TableSheet's "Follow it in The Table" closes the sheet whether or not main_open succeeded, so a failure leaves no trace on screen.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/owner/TableSheet.tsx:90 runs `s.call('main_open', …).then(onClose)` and never reads `r.ok`. Every other s.call in this context checks it (OwnerConfig.tsx:200,386; MandateEditor.tsx:228; SignSheet.tsx:292; WalletLimits.tsx:189; RescueReplay.tsx:116; RescueWatch.tsx:202,211; TableSheet.tsx:76-82: 9 of 10). Fixed: close only on ok, otherwise keep the sheet and show a WalletNotice (W.failFollow or similar in lib/words/approval.ts).

## Flow
- Owner opens a table, the deal is created, the done sheet shows
- clicks Follow it while main is unavailable -> main_open returns {ok:false}
- sheet closes anyway; nothing says the main window did not open

## Expected impact
The owner learns the deal opened but The Table did not; nothing else changes. Could break: nothing beyond the done sheet.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed main_open is shown, not swallowed
Before: 1 of 10 s.call sites in the context ignores its result (TableSheet.tsx:90)
After: 0 of 10 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the sheet needs a SessionProvider over a mock backend to render; no render harness for TableSheet exists in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: TableSheet render test under SessionProvider with a mock backend whose main_open rejects: assert the sheet stays and a notice shows (red today)

title: Every watched subscription reads "Stopping…" while one stop is pending
body:
## Summary
RescueWatch labels every row's button "Stopping…" while any rescue_watch_stop is in flight.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/owner/RescueWatch.tsx:251 renders `s.pending === 'rescue_watch_stop' ? 'Stopping…' : 'Stop watching'` on each row, with no record of which subscription was clicked. With N watched rows, N read "Stopping…". Fixed: keep the id being stopped in state and label only that row.

## Flow
- Owner watches 3 subscriptions
- clicks Stop watching on one
- all 3 buttons read Stopping… until the answer lands

## Expected impact
The owner sees which subscription is being stopped. Could break: nothing; the disabled state stays shared.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - only the clicked row says Stopping…
Before: N of N rows read Stopping… (code read: one shared pending flag)
After: 1 of N (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a SessionProvider render harness to hold a pending call
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: RescueWatch render test with a pending rescue_watch_stop over 3 rows: count buttons reading Stopping… (3 today, 1 after)

title: Rule-set tabs in the editor have tab roles but no tab keyboard pattern
body:
## Summary
MandateEditor's rule-set strip is role="tablist" with role="tab" buttons but no tabpanel, no aria-controls and no arrow-key handling.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:269-283: a screen reader announces "tab 1 of 4", and a keyboard user expects Left and Right to move between tabs (WAI-ARIA tabs). Here only Tab moves, through every tab in turn, and no panel is linked. Fixed: either add roving tabindex with arrow keys and aria-controls on the main region, or drop the tab roles and use aria-pressed buttons (what Seg does elsewhere).

## Flow
- Keyboard user focuses the first rule-set tab
- presses Right Arrow: nothing happens
- presses Tab: moves to the next tab, not into the editor

## Expected impact
Screen-reader and keyboard owners get the pattern the roles promise. Could break: focus order in the toolbar.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the roles match the keyboard behaviour
Before: 0 of 2 tab-pattern keys handled; 0 aria-controls
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - no keyboard test harness for the editor in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:269  <div className="ui-seg" role="tablist" aria-label="Agent rules">
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:275  <button … role="tab" aria-selected=… onClick=…>
instrument: render MandateEditor with two entries; fireEvent.keyDown ArrowRight on the selected tab and assert onSelect gets the next id (red today)

title: A start before 1970 or a far-future end is refused as "the end must be after the start"
body:
## Summary
buildMandate only checks end > start; Rust also refuses not_before < 0 and expires > MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and refusalWords words that refusal as "the end must be after the start".

## Description
crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs validate() refuses version 0, expires <= not_before, not_before < 0 and expires > MAX_SAFE_INTEGER with one reason, "invalid mandate version or validity". apps/desktop/client/src/lib/mandateRules.ts:51 words it "the end must be after the start", and apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/mandateDraft.ts buildMandate checks only the ordering. A 1969 start (typed into datetime-local) is refused at sign with a sentence that is false for that draft. Fixed: buildMandate refuses a start before 1970 and an end past the wallet's limit with its own field error.

## Flow
- Owner types a start of 1969-12-31 and a normal end
- what-if: REFUSED -> "These rules can’t be signed: the end must be after the start."
- the end is after the start; the message misdirects

## Expected impact
The owner is told which date is out of range. Could break: nothing for dates after 1970.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the refusal names the real cause
Before: 2 of 3 validity causes misworded (code read)
After: 0 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - a buildMandate case is the instrument; deferred for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: mandateDraft.test.ts case: buildMandate with notBefore 1969 -> ok:false with a start error (red today)

title: Market prices key is "optional" on first run and a required step afterwards
body:
## Summary
The approval window's first-run view calls the market-prices key optional, then its everyday view counts it as a thing left to set up, in gold.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/OwnerConfig.tsx:273 labels the channel3 credential "optional" and never gold while first run shows; lib/firstRun.ts START_ORDER has no market step. After first run, OwnerConfig.tsx:215-218 counts it among four required steps ("1 thing left to set up · Still to do: Market prices") and gold={!first} marks it needed. One key, two claims. Which is true is a product decision: if comparing prices is optional, drop it from `steps`/`left`; if it is needed, first run should say so.

## Flow
- New owner completes the four first-run steps without a market key (told optional)
- first-run view gives way to the everyday view
- the answer bar now reads "1 thing left to set up · Still to do: Market prices" with a gold Needed chip

## Expected impact
One consistent answer about whether the price key is needed. Could break: nothing either way.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one claim about one key
Before: 2 contradictory claims (OwnerConfig.tsx:273 vs :215-218)
After: 1
Method: probe - read both branches and lib/firstRun START_ORDER
Result: better
Gate: direction
